title: Fathom vs Umami
description: Fathom Analytics vs Umami — compare polished hosted privacy analytics vs open-source self-hostable web analytics.
verdict: Fathom (hosted) is the polished managed privacy analytics product with vendor support and a higher pageview-tier floor. Umami is the open-source / self-host path (plus Umami Cloud) for developers who want ownership and lower marginal cost at scale.
quickAnswer: **Fathom** is the better fit if you want **managed, polished privacy analytics** without running infrastructure. **Umami** is the better fit if you want **MIT open source, self-hosting (or cheap cloud), and full data ownership** and can handle ops.
bottomLine: Pick **hosted Fathom** for founders who want a clean dashboard and support, and will pay from ~$15/month for 100K pageviews. Pick **Umami** when Docker/VPS comfort is high and recurring SaaS analytics fees feel wrong. Also compare **Plausible** if you want open source plus a mature managed cloud middle ground.

faq.question: Is Fathom open source?
faq.answer: Hosted Fathom Analytics is proprietary SaaS. Fathom Lite is a separate free self-hosted product with fewer features and no vendor support — different from Umami’s MIT community model.

faq.question: Is Umami easier than Fathom?
faq.answer: Hosted Fathom is easier for non-developers. Self-hosted Umami is easier for developers who already ship Docker apps and want zero analytics SaaS lock-in.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: At low traffic, hosted Fathom’s $15/100K entry can beat some competitors’ site limits but costs more than a tiny VPS running Umami. At high traffic, self-hosted Umami often undercuts per-pageview SaaS if your time is cheap. Use the pricing calculator for SaaS tiers; add hosting for Umami self-host estimates.

faq.question: Which has better privacy?
faq.answer: Both aim at privacy-friendly web analytics. Hosted Fathom keeps data on Fathom’s cloud; Umami self-hosted keeps data on your servers. Legal review still applies for either path.

faq.question: How do scripts compare?
faq.answer: Fathom’s recorded bench is lightweight (~2.7 KiB transfer, ~+251 ms overhead). Umami’s script weight is not yet recorded on AnalyticsVS.

editorialNotes.title: Triangle with Plausible
editorialNotes.content: We already publish Plausible vs Fathom and Plausible vs Umami. This page closes the third side: managed polish (Fathom) vs open-source ownership (Umami). Many teams still land on Plausible as the default compromise.

editorialNotes.title: Affiliate status
editorialNotes.content: Fathom’s affiliate program exists but is not enabled on AnalyticsVS until signup is complete. Umami has no referral program here. See [disclosure](/disclosure/).
